recent_posts.title: My year of reading Chinese history
recent_posts.summary: A software developer shares how they fell into reading Chinese history throughout 2025, listing seven books they read. The post explores key themes discovered along the way: the cyclical nature of Chinese dynastic history versus Western linear progress narratives, the recurring tension between steppe nomads and farming civilizations, the role of imperial bureaucracy and examination systems in governance, the perennial problem of succession failure in empires, and how modern China's manufacturing dominance (Shenzhen, EVs, solar) is actually a return to historical norms rather than something new. The author draws parallels to contemporary politics and argues that learning non-Western history offers fresh perspectives on current problems.

recent_posts.title: 2025 reflections
recent_posts.summary: A software engineer reflects on 2025, covering professional growth through building a constraint solver and KCL programming language work at Zoo, speaking at four Rust conferences globally, starting Austin Systems meetup, and shifting from AI skepticism to regular usage of tools like Codex and ChatGPT for code review and debugging. Personal highlights include moving back to Austin, watching his daughter grow, reading extensively (especially Chinese history), and maintaining work-life balance through exercise and cooking.

recent_posts.title: 2024 reflections
recent_posts.summary: Adam Chalmers reflects on a year filled with personal and professional milestones, including the birth of his first child, temporary relocation to New Orleans, and speaking at multiple international conferences. He also shares his reading list and highlights some significant non-fiction books, details his continued work at Zoo on a new CAD suite, and mentions key moments like his technical podcast interview.

recent_posts.title: EuroRust 2024 talk: Code as contract as code
recent_posts.summary: Automatic schema and client generation can significantly ease API server management, as experienced by the author at Zoo compared to Cloudflare. A discussion at EuroRust 2024 highlighted different approaches to API management, emphasizing the importance of context-specific trade-offs.

recent_posts.title: RustConf 2024 talk: Building a programming language for CAD
recent_posts.summary: A presentation at RustConf 2024 discusses the development of KCL (KittyCAD language), a new programming language for 3D design. The talk covers CAD software and mechanical engineering background, the reasons for creating KCL, and insights gained from the development process.

recent_posts.title: My Developer Voices interview
recent_posts.summary: Kris Jenkins of Developer Voices interviewed the author on his podcast, discussing KittyCAD and its language, which the author is developing at Zoo. The podcast can be watched on YouTube or listened to on any podcast platform. The author praises Developer Voices for its in-depth technical discussions and recommends exploring its archive.

recent_posts.title: I'm speaking at RustConf 2024!
recent_posts.summary: The author is excited to speak at RustConf 2024 in Montreal about KCL, a 3D manufacturing language being developed at Zoo.dev. They invite other attendees to reach out and connect.

recent_posts.summary: The post discusses the development of a compiler called Grackle, which compiles to a bytecode VM called KCVM. It also mentions a presentation on KCVM and its time-travelling debugger at a tech talk event hosted by Jam.dev.
